title: What to think: a 105-question experiment plan
confirmed_choices: Reactive S2 baselines reason only when the actual user request arrives.
Pre-thinking variants generate earlier private results and reuse them.
Retain all history plus earlier results where feasible; use a documented selection fallback on overflow/OOM.
Report native thinking and ordinary output tokens separately; do not force a reasoning trace from Instruct models.
summary: Evaluate all 105 distinct questions, using verified text answers and source-based scoring facts.
Use shared chunks of about 20–45 seconds, so short fillers do not trigger separate pre-thinking calls.
Compare three S1 systems, four text-S2 families and two audio-S2 families.
Keep the user request hidden until it actually arrives, then reuse earlier private results where applicable.
Measure answer accuracy and new thinking tokens for the request, with pre-thinking tokens listed separately.
Keep full history where it fits and label every capacity fallback.

scope.reference_answer_audio: deferred; text and fact checklists suffice
scope.development: Use separate additional meetings/speakers for prompt and chunk selection; the exposed 105-question bank remains the full evaluation pool.
scope.extra_diagnostic4: The four previous text probes stay separate unless the user later expands the 105-question bank.

chunking.rule: After at least 20 elapsed seconds and eight seconds of voiced speech, close at the next completed pause of at least 0.5 seconds; target roughly 30 seconds. A hard 45-second cap bounds continuous speech.
chunking.cap_rule: At 45 seconds, close at the current causal audio frame. If speech is still continuing, mark the last speech unit partial and let the next prefix supply its continuation; do not look ahead or create a shorter retrospective chunk.
chunking.low_activity: A capped interval with less than eight seconds of speech is a passive chunk: keep all its samples in history but skip a private model call; the next active call still has that earlier audio available.
chunking.fillers: Short backchannels and fillers are accumulated with surrounding speech rather than becoming their own calls; a long low-information block may return NO_UPDATE, with its tokens counted.
chunking.request: At request onset, stop launching pre-thinking. Put the unclosed meeting tail and the complete request into the final input, even if the tail is shorter than the normal minimum.
chunking.common_schedule: Use one causal audio-VAD boundary manifest across GT text, both ASR tools and speech S2; no GT sentence boundaries or question-specific evidence may choose the cuts.
chunking.causality: A pause is used only after its silence has been observed; text prefixes include only already available words, never the complete future part of an intersecting utterance.
chunking.same_content: Macro chunks and native S1 frames cover the same original samples, request and source horizon; preserve an interval/hash ledger with no dropped or duplicated speech.
chunking.development: Compare 15/30/45 and 20/30/60 second settings on separate development meetings, then freeze one schedule for the main what-to-think study.
chunking.not_when_study: The schedule is fixed across all conditions; learned semantic trigger timing is deferred.

gold_steps: Keep one evaluation record per distinct question, verify the actual spoken request and its retained intent, and preserve requester and actual insertion time.
Reuse existing draft answers as starting material; generate a candidate answer and required-fact checklist from only the available GT prefix.
Attach source passage IDs, speaker, time, quantities/units, uncertainty and allowed alternative answers; distinguish required facts from optional context.
Check every answer with deterministic number/owner/status checks where possible, a second-model review and Codex inspection of source evidence.
Resolve disagreements and unsupported premises before freezing all 105 references; preserve versions and do not silently drop difficult cases.
Freeze answer facts and judge criteria before any evaluation run; keep them out of model inputs.
protocol: This is an unpaced content study: complete each private chunk call before releasing the next chunk; measure accuracy and token movement, without a real-time latency claim.
Pre-thinking branches see only earlier original meeting speech; synthetic evaluation questions and answers never enter the shared pre-thinking stem.

At the request, use the whole available history plus retained earlier results; user-request recognition in generated-transcript conditions comes from that tool, with a GT-question-text diagnostic reported separately.
Use the same final-answer instruction and within-model decoding/output allowance across paired conditions.
Full earlier traces and artifacts are retained when possible; chat-template stripping of previous thinking must be checked using actual serialized inputs.
Track each transcript/speaker revision at its release; do not use full-meeting future diarization or oracle speaker-name mappings in generated-transcript conditions.
Fork independent question examples from the original meeting stem; earlier synthetic questions or model replies never become history for later examples.
S2 audio experiments produce text answers and private results; native speech is scored in S1. Qualify any S2 engine that cannot separate text/reasoning from speech output.
Reuse causal pre-thinking stems per meeting/model/tool/prompt where their exact inputs match, without exposing question times to the worker.

Choose generation limits on development data: start with 8192 new tokens for native Thinking models and 4096 for Instruct, raise if needed for complete outputs, then freeze within-model paired limits and report all length stops.
The appended GT request text must match the chosen recorded question, including any retained alternative; every condition uses the same spoken request and gold intent.

After the request, allow only the fixed silence/EOS needed by native speech decoding, never resumed future meeting audio; save the full output and select scoring spans by timing rather than correctness.
capacity: Preflight audio duration, encoded positions, text length, prior-trace length and output reserve before each family.
Try full history first; reducing concurrency or a qualified larger allocation may resolve memory pressure without changing the model context limit.

When full history cannot fit, retain the request, recent complete chunks and useful earlier results; preserve older commitments, revisions and source anchors with a fixed rule using available information only.
For a paired comparison, use the same selected raw-history intervals and output reserve; list which earlier results were retained or removed.
Keep full-history and budgeted results separate while reporting an all-105 total; log selector version, omitted intervals, cause and actual input counts.

Never silently truncate, use gold evidence to select history, change precision/checkpoint, or omit a question; if even the declared minimum cannot run, record a capacity failure in the all-105 ledger.

Distinguish a model-native rolling context from caller-selected history: consuming a full recording does not prove that every earlier state remains directly accessible. Record native rolling/eviction separately from a selected-history fallback.
metrics: Primary accuracy: a complete source-supported answer without a material unsupported claim, judged using verified facts, rules and a blinded LLM judge.
Primary token measure: newly generated native thinking after the actual request, excluding all earlier pre-thinking and answer text.
For absent native thinking channels use not-applicable; for unexposed channels use unavailable, never a fabricated zero or a forced chain of thought.
Also list final-answer tokens, total request-time output, request-time input/prefill, earlier pre-thinking output, truncations and context mode.
Report native thinking means over all eligible attempts, correct-only values separately, and accuracy alongside every token comparison; silence and failed answers cannot win on token count.
Use model-specific tokenizers and compare token reductions primarily within the same model; different tokenizers and input costs prevent a universal compute interpretation.
Have the judge see the request, verified facts/source evidence and candidate answer, with model and condition names hidden; inspect disputes directly against the source.
For S1, independently transcribe generated audio and inspect disputed words/numbers by listening; an internal text stream is diagnostic, not a substitute for the spoken answer.
Report per-question logical pre-thinking exposure and the actual unique executed pre-thinking totals separately, so reuse of a shared meeting stem is not double-counted.

A helper or selector that uses the actual request performs request-time work: count its native reasoning and ordinary output, never relabel it pre-thinking. The main history selector uses fixed rules.

resources.current_dependencies: Read-only inventory/literature plus plan and report generation; no model calls, downloads or jobs.
resources.policy: All GPU jobs sequential; transcript tools and reference validation precede evaluation; judges follow generation. No concurrent S1+S2 integration is part of this matrix.
resources.qualification: Resource counts are planning envelopes, not measured fits; reuse pinned environments/checkpoints and qualify new versions before the full runs.

execution_order: Discuss and freeze this plan and notation; no inference implementation is authorized by this document alone.
Generate and validate references for all 105; select disjoint development examples.
Tune chunk thresholds and prompt goals on development data, then freeze them.
Qualify model input limits, history retention/fallback and native token extraction.
Run every selected condition on all 105 questions, including both transcript tools.
Judge answers and fill the result tables; discuss timing-policy or speech-handoff studies afterward.
